text:
Nia (design): short decision thread: we're polishing the Project -> Create form. two sticky UX questions: 1) validation behavior for dense rows (users can add 20+ lines)  show per-field inline errors as they type, or present a compact error summary at top after submit? 2) required-field signal: tiny asterisk only, or explicit 'Required' label visible?
Cal (pm): for power users i prefer a top summary + jump-to-first-error after submit. inline is noisy in table-like flows. for single resource flow, inline is nicer.
Ivy (frontend): perf note: every inline error node costs paint and increases layout thrash when validation runs over 50 rows. we can lazy-mount the inline copy when a cell receives focus or after the first submit attempt.
Omar (a11y): accessibility: asterisk alone is risky. screen readers don't always announce it. recommend visible 'Required' for key fields or set aria-required=true and include a visually-hidden 'Required' tied to the input. also put aria-live="polite" on the top summary so SRs hear the result without interruption.
Nia (design): copy tone: current inline says "Name required". i'd like a short, friendly template: "Please enter a name for this project." keeps it actionable.
Cal (pm): agree on friendlier copy. regarding destructive actions: typed-confirm (type resource name) vs undo toast. typed confirm for irreversible customer data deletion, undo for accidental single-item deletes if we support restore.
Ivy (frontend): typed-confirm is heavier to implement (focus + prevent accidental keyboard submits). undo toast is lighter but depends on backend retention policies. both are doable; we should document which flows use which pattern.
Omar (a11y): typed-confirm must set role=dialog, aria-modal=true, focus the input, and announce the exact phrase to type. avoid surprise focus shifts for screen reader users; include keyboard alternatives.
Nia (design): proposed pattern: summary-first after submit showing "We found X issues" with anchors. inline errors appear when a user focuses a field or after blur. required marker: show an asterisk visually but also include a visually-hidden "Required" label connected via aria-describedby. tooltip on hover for sighted users.
Cal (pm): sounds pragmatic. let's add a small rule: fields that gate provisioning (like "Region" or "Billing ID") should show visible 'Required' rather than only an asterisk.
Ivy (frontend): implementation plan: add aria-live polite to summary, lazy-create inline nodes on focus, and expose an API flag on our form component to toggle visible 'Required' for critical fields. i'll prototype a PR and measure render with a 200-row dataset.
Omar (a11y): also add a skip-link target so keyboard users can jump straight to the error summary. anchors should move focus to the affected input and announce "Error in [field name]: [error message]" via aria-live.
Nia (design): quick poll: react :one: for inline-eager (show inline as errors occur) or :two: for summary-first (summary then inline-on-focus).
RedwoodBot: New reaction: :eyes:
Cal (pm): :two:
Ivy (frontend): :one: (but can adapt)
Omar (a11y): :two:
Nia (design): summary-first wins in this thread. i'll mock two variants (summary-first + inline-on-focus, and inline-eager) and run a 6-person usability check including one screen-reader participant. tagging @Ivy for feasibility and @Omar for a11y review before final copy rollout. will post prototypes by tomorrow afternoon. :sparkles:
